name: @xenosisorg/xenosis-mcp

tools.name: get_peer_graph
tools.description: Returns the full peer mesh of this Xenosis workspace plus any boundary violations. Use this to answer "why does service A get 403 from service B" — check `violations` for the caller→callee pair, then look at the callee's `allowedCallers` (in get_service_config) to see who is permitted. A common cause is a mismatched `peerName` (the caller identifies itself with one name but the callee expects another).

tools.name: get_service_config
tools.description: Returns the parsed xenosis.config.json of one service with secrets redacted (tokens, JWT secrets, DB credentials masked). Use this to inspect peer identity (`peerName`), declared peers, `boundaries.allowedCallers`, the auth gate, and OpenAPI/connector/schema bindings. Service name matches `peerName`, `name`, or directory.

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: Hits GET /healthcheck on each service's local port. Returns up/down + response time. "down" usually means the service is not running (start with `xenosis dev`) or crashed at boot. Omit `service` to check all.

service.description: Optional service identifier. Omit to check every service.

tools.name: get_openapi_spec
tools.description: Fetches the OpenAPI 3.1 spec of a running service. Returns a summary by default (paths + methods + operation summaries) which is enough for most questions; set `full: true` for the entire JSON. The service must be running (start with `xenosis dev`).

full.description: Return the full spec instead of a summary (can be large).

tools.name: explain_trace
tools.description: Given an x-xenosis-trace-id, returns every peer call (with request/response bodies, durations, statuses) and every log line that mentioned the same id, across all services. Use this to diagnose failures that span multiple services. Requires `xenosis dev` to be running.

traceId.description: The x-xenosis-trace-id (UUID) emitted by the request-context middleware.

tools.name: simulate_change
tools.description: Returns the callers of a service (its blast radius), which boundary permissions are in play, and where consumer-side code likely lives. Use this BEFORE proposing edits to a service's request/response schema or its allowedCallers list so you can name every caller that will need updating in the same PR.

service.description: The target service — peerName, config.name, or directory.

method.description: Optional peer method name (e.g. "createCharge"). When provided, returned hint paths narrow to controller files mentioning it.

addCaller.description: Optional: a service name you're proposing to ADD as a caller. The tool reports whether the target's boundaries would currently refuse it.

tools.name: get_event_graph
tools.description: Returns the async event mesh of this Xenosis workspace: which services publish to which topics, which services consume them, and which topics have no producer / no consumer. Mirrors `xenosis graph --events --json`. Use this to answer "who emits charge.succeeded?" or "what reacts when order.created fires?" — check `apis[<n>].producersByTopic[<topicKey>]` and `consumersByTopic[<topicKey>]`. Orphan topics (in `orphans`) signal a producer with no consumer; unserved consumers (in `unservedConsumers`) signal a handler that depends on a topic nobody emits in this workspace. Source data: each service's xenosis.config.json `events` block + the `defineEventApi(...)` packages they reference + a static scan of `src/events/*.event.ts` for handler registrations.
